surface: AGENTS.md, .plate platform, import-payload, bootstrap, template validators
summary: Adds a .plate platform setting that selects which PLATE-owned scripts import and bootstrap copy, and which GIF scripts validation requires
migration_impact: Schema 1.3 adds optional top-level platform: posix, posix-and-windows, or windows. A missing key migrates to posix and means import-payload and bootstrap omit PLATE-owned .ps1 twins. posix-and-windows copies both flavors and validation requires both GIF scripts. windows omits PLATE-owned .sh twins, rewrites the copied template CI test job to pwsh -File scripts/ValidatePlateRepo.ps1 -Root . on windows-latest, and points the copied process-gifs job at gif-from-video.ps1 through pwsh. Existing destination files are not deleted. Adopter-owned scripts are outside the PLATE basename filter. PLATE itself sets posix-and-windows. --platform overrides .plate for that run and is persisted on apply. Invalid values fail closed. The operator OS is not consulted.
migration_guidance: 1. Set .plate platform to posix (default when absent), posix-and-windows, or windows. Do not infer it from the operator machine, Windows dependencies, or CI host.

2. import-payload and bootstrap --apply copy PLATE-owned script twins for that value only. posix omits .ps1. windows omits .sh and rewrites package.json record:e2e to pwsh -File scripts/e2e-record.ps1. posix-and-windows copies both. Namespaced copies retarget PLATE script paths inside copied scripts and package.json to scripts/plate/. scripts/README.md and scripts/dev-server.js always copy. Pass --platform to override .plate; apply writes the value back. A remote .plate that is not valid JSON fails bootstrap instead of being read as posix. An empty or whitespace-only platform string is invalid in every reader, including an explicit --platform, and does not fall through to the stored value. JSON null loads as posix. When --platform is set and a remote .plate already exists, bootstrap parses that file before copying templates.

3. Validation follows the same value and accepts scripts/ or scripts/plate/. posix requires gif-from-video.sh. posix-and-windows requires both GIF scripts and template CI stays on the shell validator. windows requires gif-from-video.ps1, the copied CI job runs ValidatePlateRepo.ps1 on windows-latest, and the copied process-gifs job calls gif-from-video.ps1 through pwsh. The PowerShell validator rejects a non-string platform, including a one-element array, the same way the shell validator does.

4. Do not delete scripts with a *.ps1 or *.sh glob. The filter is basename-only for PLATE twins (validate_plate_repo.sh, ValidatePlateRepo.ps1, bootstrap_github.sh, BootstrapGitHub.ps1, check_toolchain.sh, CheckToolchain.ps1, question_batch.sh, QuestionBatch.ps1, e2e-record.sh, e2e-record.ps1, gif-from-video.sh, gif-from-video.ps1) at scripts/ or scripts/plate/.
5. Dual-stack repositories, including PLATE, set platform to posix-and-windows so both flavors stay. The template payload on disk remains the superset; the destination platform decides the copy.
agent_notes: Read .plate platform before authoring or copying scripts. Absent or JSON null means posix: author and copy .sh only. An empty string is invalid. posix-and-windows: .sh is primary and each operator-facing script also has a .ps1. windows: .ps1 only, copied template CI uses ValidatePlateRepo.ps1 on windows-latest, and the copied process-gifs job calls gif-from-video.ps1 through pwsh. Never infer platform from the laptop OS. --platform is an explicit human instruction and must be persisted on apply. When a remote .plate already exists, parse it before copying templates. Omit PLATE-owned twins from the copy set; do not delete files already in the destination and do not touch adopter-owned scripts. Invalid platform values fail closed.
